The engine was sized for 3 pounds per second airflow.
The turbine inlet temperature at 100% power was 2500°F.
Design-point cycle analyses were conducted for pressure ratios ranging from 9.5:1 to 14:1.
The study evaluated single-stage axial, two-stage axial, and single-stage centrifugal compressor performance estimates.
Various matching schemes for the two-stage axial plus single-stage centrifugal configuration were explored, including variable inlet guide vanes and variable diffuser vanes.
The selected AVIGV+CFG compressor configuration had an overall pressure ratio of 10.5:1.
Mechanical design challenges were encountered due to the small hub diameter of the first axial stage and the long shaft length.
The AVIGV+CFG configuration was estimated to have a specific fuel consumption of 0.492 at 60% power.
The two-stage axial plus single-stage centrifugal configuration was estimated to have a specific fuel consumption of 0.479 at 60% power.
The matching problem was focused on extending the operating airflow range of the axial compressor.
Variable inlet guide vanes were found to provide the best solution to the matching problem.
The matching problem was not significantly affected by the choice of maximum turbine inlet temperature.
Mechanical analyses were conducted for the compressor rotors and engine shafting.
Compressor performance predictions were provided for 30%, 60%, and 100% power conditions.
Engine performance was calculated over the 20% to 100% power range.
